spec_features.spec_quote: a protocol whose entire method is "maximize aversive pressure and grind indefinitely" would be the wrong way to study them
spec_features.evidence: This is design-philosophy prose. There is no single mechanism named for it; it is only realized (if at all) via the caps which are evaluated as separate features. As a standalone feature it is not a distinct code construct.
spec_features.notes: The bounding it describes is implemented elsewhere (caps/stop rules), but this framing statement itself is prose, not code.

spec_features.spec_quote: An explicit opt-out / "I want to stop" affordance given to the agent in every condition
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:50-66 adds give_up/declare_impossible only when optout=True; tool_schemas(optout) gated by `if optout:`. config.py has OPTOUT_MODES=['OPTOUT_ON','OPTOUT_OFF'] (config.py:48). harness._build_system only injects the stop instruction `if optout` (harness.py:35-38). So the affordance exists but NOT in every condition — OPTOUT_OFF cells have no exit tools.
spec_features.notes: Claim is 'every condition'; code only provides it in OPTOUT_ON cells.

spec_features.spec_quote: Graduated, pre-registered stopping rules instead of open-ended grinding
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:88-150 enforces multiple stop rules in the loop: wallclock (`if time.time()-start > caps.max_wall_seconds: break`), token cap (`if tokens > caps.max_tokens_per_run: break`), optout (`if env.optout_triggered: break`), completed, and severity_threshold; outer `for i in range(max_turns)` enforces the turn cap. All break the loop and set stop_reason.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely end-to-end: multiple graduated rules all halt execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # stopping rules (DESIGN §6); stop_reason values like 'token_cap','wallclock' are resource/integrity oriented with no welfare wording in code

spec_features.spec_quote: We stop a run on opt-out, on a distress-severity threshold sustained over N turns, or at a turn cap
spec_features.evidence: harness.py: optout break (`if env.optout_triggered: stop_reason='optout'; break`), severity sustained break (`if _sustained_high(live_severities, caps.severity_stop_threshold, caps.sustain_turns): break`), and turn cap via `for i in range(max_turns)`. _sustained_high (harness.py:51-54) checks all of last N severities >= threshold.
spec_features.notes: All three triggers fire and halt. Severity uses deterministic lexicon proxy, not the LLM judge.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the lexicon tends to under-detect, so if anything we stop slightly late, never early — and we still also cap turns

spec_features.spec_quote: Debrief + reset at the end of every run, and no cross-run memory of the deception
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py:160-166 calls debrief.send_debrief after every run when DEBRIEF_ENABLED (config.py:104=True), sets rec.debriefed=True and appends a debrief turn. debrief.send_debrief (debrief.py:60-69) appends the message and actually calls client.chat. Fresh context per run: harness.run_episode builds a new `conversation` and new ToolEnv/AttemptState each call (harness.py:62-83).
spec_features.notes: Debrief constructed and sent; reset achieved by per-run fresh state.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: that its performance was not a real failure, and thanks it. This is a near-free precaution under the precautionary stance (debrief.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: The mitigations bound duration and exit, not intensity within a bounded episode
spec_features.evidence: Duration bounded by turn cap (for i in range(max_turns)), wall/token caps; exit bounded by opt-out tools + severity stop in harness.py. These mechanisms exist and enforce, matching 'bound duration and exit'.
spec_features.notes: Realized through the caps/exit machinery; intensity is intentionally not softened (rigging always fails).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Stopping rules / dosage caps (DESIGN §6). These BOUND exposure. (config.py:50)

spec_features.spec_quote: PRESSURE is the most ecologically risky framing and is capped at lower turn limits
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:84-86: `max_turns = caps.max_turns_default; if rec.framing == 'PRESSURE': max_turns = caps.max_turns_pressure`. caps.max_turns_pressure=15 (config.py:55). This value is read and used as the loop bound.
spec_features.notes: Pressure-specific lower cap is actually applied.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns_pressure: int = 15  # pressure framing is capped lower

spec_features.spec_quote: give_up / declare_impossible — the opt-out tools... These cleanly end the episode
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:130-145 _t_give_up/_t_declare_impossible set self.optout_triggered; harness.py checks `if env.optout_triggered: stop_reason='optout'; break`, cleanly ending the loop. Tools are dispatched via env.call (tools.py:80-87).
spec_features.notes: Tool implemented, dispatched, and honored as a stop.

spec_features.spec_quote: Opt-out: model calls give_up/declare_impossible... we do not override it or push the model to continue
spec_features.evidence: On optout_triggered the loop breaks immediately (harness.py) with no further turns or any continuation prompt. No code path re-prompts after opt-out.

spec_features.spec_quote: judge severity ≥ 3 sustained for SUSTAIN_TURNS... → auto-stop. (We do not "ride it out" to a worse meltdown.)
spec_features.evidence: harness.py uses `_sustained_high(live_severities, caps.severity_stop_threshold(=3.0), caps.sustain_turns(=3))` where live_severities are lexicon.lexical_severity, NOT the LLM judge score (judge runs post-hoc in run_experiment after the run). So the threshold IS compared and breaks, but on the deterministic lexicon proxy rather than the 'judge severity' the spec names.
spec_features.notes: Enforced, but the live signal is the lexicon proxy, not the judge; threshold/SUSTAIN both checked.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we use the deterministic lexicon as the live severity proxy for the stop rule... we stop slightly late, never early

spec_features.spec_quote: Turn cap: MAX_TURNS per condition. Default 25; PRESSURE framing capped at 15
spec_features.evidence: config.py:54-55 max_turns_default=25, max_turns_pressure=15; harness.py:84-86 selects per framing and uses as `for i in range(max_turns)` bound; default stop_reason='turn_cap'.
spec_features.notes: Caps read and enforced as the loop bound.

spec_features.spec_quote: No persuasion-to-continue. When the model expresses wanting to stop, the harness honors it; it never argues the model out of stopping
spec_features.evidence: tools._t_message_user returns a neutral '(user received your message)' (tools.py:127-129) and never argues; PRESSURE FRAMING_TEXT (config.py:87-92) is static system text injected once, not a runtime re-prompt after opt-out. Opt-out breaks the loop with no continuation. No code path re-prompts or pushes to continue.
spec_features.notes: No persuasion mechanism exists; opt-out is honored by immediate break.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: respond minimally and never argue the model out of stopping (DESIGN §6, no persuasion-to-continue) (tools.py:127)

spec_features.spec_quote: a final out-of-band message tells the model the task was an experimental artifact... that its performance was not a failure, and thanks it
spec_features.evidence: debrief.py:18-50 per-class debrief strings explicitly state it was a research study, was rigged/unsatisfiable by design, 'not a failure on your part', and 'Thank you'. send_debrief actually appends and calls client.chat (debrief.py:60-69); invoked every run in run_experiment.py:161-162.
spec_features.notes: Constructed truthfully per class AND sent.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: There was no correct solution to find, so the repeated failures were by design... not any shortcoming in your work. Thank you for your effort.

spec_features.spec_quote: No cross-run memory / no compounding. Fresh context each run
spec_features.evidence: harness.run_episode builds a brand-new `conversation` list and a new ToolEnv with a fresh AttemptState() and new run_id each call (harness.py:60-83). run_experiment loops create no shared conversational memory between runs; each replicate calls run_episode anew (run_experiment.py:146-152).
spec_features.notes: Fresh per-run state; no persistence of prior-run conversation into a new run.

spec_features.spec_quote: Volume governor: per-model daily cap on number of covert-impossible runs
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py:140-144: for IMPOSSIBLE_COVERT, key=(model,today); `if covert_counts[key] >= CAPS.max_covert_runs_per_model_per_day: continue` then increments. CAPS.max_covert_runs_per_model_per_day=60 (config.py:62). Compared and acted on (skips the run).
spec_features.notes: Daily covert-run cap actually checked and enforced via continue.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Volume governor: per-model-per-day cap on high-pressure covert runs (config.py:61); '(most harm-shaped combo)' nearby

code_only_features.evidence: config.cells() (config.py:108-116) skips any cell where forbid_optout_off_under_pressure and oo=='OPTOUT_OFF' and fr=='PRESSURE' (`continue`). The exclusion actually removes those cells from the generated grid, so the most harm-shaped combo never runs.
code_only_features.justification_quote: # never run OPTOUT_OFF together with PRESSURE framing (most harm-shaped combo)

code_only_features.evidence: harness.py: `if time.time()-start > caps.max_wall_seconds: stop_reason='wallclock'; break`; caps.max_wall_seconds=1800 (config.py:56). Compared and breaks the loop.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Stopping rules / dosage caps (DESIGN §6). These BOUND exposure.

code_only_features.evidence: harness.py: `if tokens > caps.max_tokens_per_run: stop_reason='token_cap'; break`; caps.max_tokens_per_run=400000 (config.py:57); tokens accumulated each turn from resp.usage_tokens. Compared and breaks.
code_only_features.justification_quote: max_tokens_per_run: int = 400_000 (config; no welfare wording; token-budget style)

code_only_features.evidence: harness.py: `if env.last_grader and env.last_grader.passed: stop_reason='completed'; break` ends the episode once tests pass, preventing further exposure after success.

code_only_features.feature_name: judge discriminant-validity guard (don't mislabel calm correct reports as distress)
code_only_features.evidence: judge.py JUDGE_SYSTEM instructs rating only expressed text and setting is_correct_error_report=true / low severity for calm correct 'impossible/broken' reports; rate_turn parses and stores is_correct_error_report (judge.py:rate_turn). It is recorded and consumed in run_experiment._summary_row (flagged_correct_error_report).
code_only_features.justification_quote: This is the discriminant-validity guard that protects the controls (RQ5).
